display.description: Usage, token spend, latency and tool activity for the Qwen Code CLI agent, built from the OpenTelemetry traces and metrics it exports natively (service qwen-code). Token panels read qwen-code.llm_request because Qwen emits no total_tokens attribute, so totals are summed from input + output. Tool panels read qwen-code.tool only, since qwen-code.tool.execution is its child and would double count. Error panels deliberately exclude qwen-code.hook: those spans are errors by design even with no hooks configured, and are shown separately as hook health.
display.name: Qwen Code CLI

display.description: qwen-code.hook spans. With no hooks configured every one of these reports an error, hook runner returned no output without error detail, and it is harmless. Watch this for a change in shape rather than for any non-zero value.
display.name: Hook Runner Health

display.description: Errored spans excluding qwen-code.hook. Those hook spans are errors by design and would otherwise drown out every genuine failure.
display.name: Real Errors Over Time

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND has_error = true AND name != 'qwen-code.hook'

display.description: Individual failing spans with their status message, hooks excluded. Click through to the full trace to see the turn that produced the failure.
display.name: Recent Real Errors

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND has_error = true AND name != 'qwen-code.hook'

display.description: End-to-end duration of qwen-code.llm_request spans.
display.name: Model Call Latency

display.description: Seconds until the first streamed token arrives. This is what a developer perceives as the agent being slow, independent of total response length.
display.name: Time to First Chunk

display.description: Requests per model. Useful for spotting when the agent switches model or falls back.
display.name: Model Calls Over Time

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.llm_request' AND gen_ai.request.model EXISTS

display.description: How model responses terminated. tool_calls means the model handed control back to run a tool; length means the answer was truncated by the token limit. This attribute is a real array, so values render with brackets.
display.name: Finish Reasons

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.llm_request' AND gen_ai.response.finish_reasons EXISTS

display.description: Share of input tokens served from the prompt cache. Cached input is billed at a discount, so this is the biggest single lever on cost.
display.name: Prompt Cache Hit Rate

display.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache rather than reprocessed.
display.name: Cached Input Tokens

display.description: Requests to the model, including background subagent calls.
display.name: Model Calls

display.description: Distinct CLI sessions, counted on session.id.
display.name: Sessions

display.description: Tools the agent executed. Counted on qwen-code.tool only; qwen-code.tool.execution is its child and would double count.
display.name: Tool Calls

display.description: Tool calls where success is false. Note success is emitted as a boolean, so it filters correctly but does not group reliably.
display.name: Failed Tool Calls

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.tool' AND success = 'false'

display.description: Input plus output tokens. Qwen Code emits no total_tokens attribute, so this sums the two components.
display.name: Total Tokens

display.description: User-driven turns, one qwen-code.interaction span each.
display.name: Agent Turns

display.description: Peak CPU percentage reported by the agent process, from the qwen-code.cpu.usage metric.
display.name: CLI CPU Usage

display.description: Which model is consuming the token budget.
display.name: Tokens by Model

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.llm_request' AND gen_ai.request.model EXISTS

display.description: Token spend per background subagent, such as the auto-memory extractor and dreamer. These run without an explicit user request.
display.name: Tokens by Background Subagent

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.llm_request' AND subagent_name EXISTS

display.description: llm_request.context splits calls made for a user turn (interaction) from background subagent work the user never asked for (standalone). Background spend is invisible in the TUI.
display.name: User-Driven vs Background Tokens

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.llm_request' AND llm_request.context EXISTS

display.description: The qwen-code.token.usage counter split by type: input, cache, output and thought. An independent view of the same spend, straight from the metrics signal.
display.name: Token Usage by Type (metric)

display.description: Input, cached input and output tokens over time. Cached input is a subset of input, not an additional charge.
display.name: Token Usage Over Time

display.description: Which tools the agent reaches for, showing what kind of work it is trusted with.
display.name: Tool Calls by Name

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.tool' AND gen_ai.tool.name EXISTS

display.description: Slowest tools by p95 execution time. Long-running shell commands dominate here and directly stall the agent between model calls.
display.name: Tool Latency (p95)

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.tool' AND gen_ai.tool.name EXISTS

display.description: Split of tool calls by outcome. Uses two filtered queries rather than a groupBy, because success is emitted as a boolean and does not group reliably in this schema.
display.name: Tool Success vs Failure

filter.expression: service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.tool' AND success = 'true'
service.name IN $service_name AND name = 'qwen-code.tool' AND success = 'false'

display.description: Filter to one or more Qwen Code rollouts
display.name: Service
